paras_en: USD/JPY

U.S. November consumer confidence rose to its highest since January last year, boosting the dollar. Insiders said the U.S. Trade Representative office is preparing a survey targeting sixteen major trading partners, including China and the EU, over alleged industrial overcapacity and is expected to impose new import tariffs on a wide range of goods. The fresh tariff threat dampened market sentiment, halted the AI‑related tech rally, triggered a sharp sell‑off in Asian equities and added safe‑haven demand for the dollar. Meanwhile, BOJ data showed Japan’s service‑producer price index for October rose 4.2% year‑on‑year – the fastest pace since 1990 – indicating expanding inflation pressure and strengthening the case for a near‑term rate hike. TBS reported that the Japanese government is not considering issuing new deficit‑financing bonds for this fiscal year, leaving the yen without support and putting pressure on the dollar/yen pair near the 159.50 high.

Subsequent U.S. data showed initial jobless claims fell to 189,000. October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% from the previous month and 3.8% year‑on‑year, reviving inflation concerns and bolstering expectations that the Fed may keep raising rates into early next year. October new‑home sales jumped 14.2% month‑over‑month to an annualised 701,000, the highest since December 2022, and Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3%, the fastest in three years. The Fed’s latest Beige Book noted the economy is growing at a modest pace, but input‑cost inflation exceeds price gains, squeezing corporate profits. The dollar, affected by AI‑related capital flows and growth expectations, fell to a low of 158.64 against the yen. The dollar/yen resistance is projected at 159.30‑50 with support at 158.30‑50 today.
EUR/USD

Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed rising international oil prices lifted fuel costs, pushing October CPI up 0.5% month‑on‑month and 4.9% year‑on‑year. Ex‑fuel core CPI rose 3.8% from a year ago, ending a few months of a steady 3.6% trend, indicating persistent inflation pressure. This cooled expectations of a RBA rate cut next year and nudged the Aussie up slightly, but a sharp Asian equity sell‑off hurt risk appetite and copper fell to an 11‑month low, limiting the Aussie’s rise and dragging the euro/dollar down to a 1.0930 low.

As the new U.S. tariff threat sparked safe‑haven buying, Germany reported September export and retail sales weaker than initially estimated and Q3 GDP grew only 0.1% versus the prior quarter, below the preliminary figure. France’s November consumer confidence rose as expected to 82, and the spread between the 10‑year U.S. and German bond yields narrowed. Ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, the euro rallied to a 1.0992 high against the dollar. Euro/dollar support is seen at 1.0930‑50 with resistance at 1.1020‑40 today.
GBP/USD

A Nvidia‑driven market rally proved fleeting; by Wednesday risk‑off sentiment returned. Ahead of key U.S. inflation data and the Thanksgiving break, investors trimmed risk‑asset exposure, pushing sterling down to a 1.3043 low against the dollar. Later, BOE Governor Andrew Bailey said that if energy prices stay stable, the inflation peak could be lower, but he leans toward further rate hikes. MPC member Swati Dhingra called for larger and earlier hikes, lifting the pound to a 1.3131 high. Today’s pound/dollar support is projected at 1.3075‑95 with resistance at 1.3170‑90.

items.title_en: New York FX Market: Dollar Weakens, AI Stock Volatility Sparks Safe‑Haven Buying, Boosting Yen and Franc
paras: 美元週三(25日)走弱，AI相關股票大幅下挫，隨後又收復大部分早盤跌幅，市場經歷劇烈震盪，避險貨幣瑞士法郎與日元走強。
科技股占比較高的那斯達克綜合指數一度因AI概念股再度遭遇賣壓而下跌約4%，隨後反彈，終場跌幅收斂至約0.6%。
美元稍早受惠於市場避險情緒升溫，但在交易時段後段轉為下跌。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.22%，報103.62。
investingLive首席外匯分析師Adam Button表示，股市出現「大幅反攻」。「我想知道，這是否只是因假期縮短交易週而出現的空頭回補行情，但即使是最糟的情況，這至少也是市場重新展現活力的訊號。」
美國大多數市場週四將因感恩節假期休市。
過去股市下跌時，美元一直扮演避險貨幣的角色，但同時受到與AI投資熱潮相關的資金流入及經濟成長預期影響。
歐元兌美元上漲0.17%，至1.0983美元。
日元兌美元上漲0.06%，至1美元兌159.13日元。
美元兌瑞士法郎下跌0.63%，至0.83瑞郎。
對風險較敏感的澳幣下跌0.15%，至0.6628美元，稍早一度跌至0.6557美元，創12月3日以來最低。
交易員也正評估，聯準會(Fed)在持續面臨高於理想水準的通膨之際，未來可能還會升息幾次。
美國10月通膨進一步升溫，個人消費支出(PCE)物價指數上月上漲0.3%，9月則維持先前公布的0.5%增幅。排除波動較大的食品及能源價格後，核心PCE物價指數上月也上漲0.3%，與9月未經修正的0.3%增幅相同。
然而，隨著近期油價下跌，市場通膨預期近幾週已經回落。
CIBC Capital Markets外匯策略主管Sarah Ying表示，「更重要的問題在於，你認為最終利率會落在什麼水準？這也是為什麼你會看到5年期債券表現略優於2年期債券，因為大部分相關疑問都集中在較長期，而不一定是可預見的未來。」
美國2年期與5年期公債殖利率曲線已趨於平坦，目前利差約為2個基點，相較之下，上個月利差一度高達27個基點。市場預期聯準會可能進一步升息，對利率敏感的2年期公債殖利率因此承壓。
另一方面，市場對川普政府週三提出、針對14個主要貿易夥伴商品加徵新關稅的計畫反應不大。這些關稅措施旨在因應美方所稱的結構性工業產能過剩，其中中國將面臨最高稅率。華府認為，中國是以低價出口商品充斥全球市場的主要責任方。中國則駁斥這項指控，表示其出口反映的是自身競爭優勢。
美國貿易代表葛里爾(Jamieson Greer)週三接受CNBC訪問時表示，擬議的新關稅大致維持既有貿易協議所設定的稅率，部分稅率可能再提高幾個百分點。
Ying表示，市場早已預期這些關稅措施，因此並未對市場造成影響。「這並不是第二次『解放日』。」
其他方面，歐元區政策制定者Olaf Sleijpen週二表示，歐洲央行(ECB)可能在12月調升政策利率，但此後的利率走向仍不明朗。
英國央行(BoE)總裁Andrew Bailey表示，如果國際能源價格在近期下跌後維持目前水準，英國通膨可能不會像本月稍早預測的那麼高。
在日本，官方數據顯示，衡量服務業通膨的重要指標10月年增4.2%，顯示價格壓力正在擴大，也進一步支持日本央行(BoJ)近期升息的理由。

paras_en: The dollar weakened on Wednesday (the 25th), as AI‑related stocks plunged sharply before later recouping most of their early‑session losses, leaving the market highly volatile and pushing safe‑haven currencies the Swiss franc and the yen higher.

The Nasdaq Composite, which has a high weighting of technology stocks, fell about 4% at one point as AI‑theme shares came under renewed selling pressure, then rebounded, ending the session with a modest decline of roughly 0.6%.
The dollar had earlier benefited from rising market safe‑haven sentiment but turned lower in the latter part of the trading session.
In the New York close, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, slipped 0.22% to 103.62.

InvestingLive chief FX analyst Adam Button said the equity market saw a “large counter‑attack.” “I wonder whether this is merely a short‑covering rally caused by the shortened trading week due to the holiday, but even in the worst case it at least signals that the market is regaining some vigor,” he added.
Most U.S. markets will be closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
In past market sell‑offs the dollar has acted as a safe‑haven currency, yet it is also influenced by capital flows tied to the AI investment boom and expectations for economic growth.
The euro rose 0.17% against the dollar to $1.0983.
The yen gained 0.06% versus the dollar, trading at 159.13 yen per $1.
The dollar fell 0.63% against the Swiss franc, to 0.83 franc.
The risk‑sensitive Australian dollar slipped 0.15% to $0.6628, after briefly touching $0.6557 earlier, its lowest level since December 3.
Traders are also assessing that the Federal Reserve, still facing inflation above its target, may raise rates a few more times.

U.S. October inflation further accelerated, with the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index up 0.3% month‑over‑month, after a 0.5% rise in September. Excluding the more volatile food and energy components, the core PCE price index also rose 0.3% last month, matching September’s unadjusted 0.3% gain.
However, with recent declines in oil prices, market inflation expectations have retreated over the past few weeks.

CIBC Capital Markets head of FX strategy Sarah Ying said, “The more important question is what level you think the ultimate interest rate will settle at. That’s why you see the 5‑year bond performing slightly better than the 2‑year, because most of the uncertainty is concentrated in the longer end rather than the near‑term foreseeable future.”

The yield curve between U.S. 2‑year and 5‑year Treasury bonds has flattened, with the spread now about 2 basis points, compared with a peak of 27 basis points last month. Market expectations of further Fed hikes are putting pressure on the rate‑sensitive 2‑year yields.

On the other hand, markets gave little reaction to the Trump administration’s Wednesday proposal to impose new tariffs on goods from 14 major trading partners. The tariffs are intended to address what the U.S. calls structural overcapacity in industry, with China facing the highest rates. Washington argues that China is the primary source of low‑priced exports that flood global markets. China has rejected the accusation, saying its exports reflect its own competitive advantages.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Wednesday that the proposed new tariffs would largely maintain the rates set under existing trade agreements, with some duties possibly rising a few percentage points.
Ying noted that the market had already priced in these tariff measures, so they did not move markets. “This is not a second ‘Liberation Day.’”
Elsewhere, Eurozone policy‑maker Olaf Sleijpen said on Tuesday that the European Central Bank may raise its policy rate in December, but the subsequent rate path remains unclear.

Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey said that if international energy prices stay at current levels after recent declines, UK inflation may not be as high as earlier this month’s forecasts suggested.

In Japan, official data showed that the key service‑sector inflation gauge rose 4.2% year‑over‑year in October, indicating expanding price pressure and further supporting the Bank of Japan’s recent rate‑hike rationale.

items.title_en: U.S. Stocks Slide, Ripple Through Forex! Carry‑Trade Gains Shrink, Wall Street Raises Alerts
paras: 美股AI交易降溫，衝擊正延伸至匯市。過去受惠於利差、經濟韌性與低波動環境的外匯套利交易(carry trade)，如今也面臨考驗。儘管部分策略今年報酬一度接近20%，隨著市場震盪加劇，華爾街認為，輕鬆獲利的階段可能已經過去。
據《彭博》報導，套利交易是指投資人借入日元、歐元或美元等利率相對較低的貨幣，再投入收益較高的市場，賺取利差。不過，一旦投資標的貨幣貶值，匯損就可能迅速侵蝕累積的利息收益。

套利仍有獲利 華爾街提醒不能買了就不管

過去一年多，利差夠大、經濟成長穩健，加上股市走高與長時間低波動，讓套利交易即使遭遇伊朗戰爭、日元干預及土耳其政治醜聞引發的市場動盪，仍能維持表現。
但近期AI交易出現裂痕，削弱風險偏好並推升波動，對仰賴平穩市場的套利策略形成壓力。
Brandywine Global Investment Management投資組合經理Tracy Chen表示：「這筆交易最容易賺錢的階段，可能已經過去了。我不會說套利交易結束了，而是持有這些部位的門檻提高了。」
套利交易整體仍有獲利。《彭博》一項指標顯示，截至周二，以歐元融資的一籃子新興市場部位，今年來報酬仍達13%；以美元融資的策略，過去兩年報酬則約18%。不過，這些報酬已較幾周前縮水，經理人對2027年能否再現亮眼表現，也更為審慎。
高盛(GS-US)認為，經過多年強勁表現後，套利交易大幅獲利的空間已更有限。花旗集團(C-US)美國外匯交易團隊則提醒，不能把套利視為建立部位後就能放著不管的交易。

巴西幣單日重挫8% 年內18%報酬幾乎吐光

巴西就是風險迅速浮現的例子。當地雙位數利率，原本讓巴西成為套利交易熱門目的地，但總統魯拉在決選中擊敗市場偏好的Flavio Bolsonaro後，巴西幣單日重挫8%，創逾20年最大跌幅，促使投資人平倉。
決選前，買進巴西幣、賣出美元的部位，今年來報酬曾達18%；截至周二，累積報酬卻只剩0.5%。
貝萊德(BLK-US)新興市場債券團隊投資組合經理Pablo Goldberg形容，套利交易「獲利像爬樓梯，回吐卻像搭電梯往下」。他提醒，若部位集中於單一貨幣，就必須格外留意風險。
不過，支持套利交易的條件尚未完全消失。即使美股近期下跌，標普500與那斯達克100指數今年仍維持漲勢，有望連續第四年收高。摩根大通(JPM-US)追蹤的外匯波動指標雖然上升，也仍明顯低於3月底的多月高點。

銀行轉向挑選貨幣 搭配日元部位避險

摩根大通策略師預期，套利交易在2027年仍能發揮作用，但表現將更容易受到股市波動，以及市場對Fed最終政策利率預期變化的影響。
因此，該行建議投資人搭配防禦性避險，例如買進日元、賣出紐西蘭元或瑞士法郎，而非單純押注利差收益。
富國銀行(WFC-US)對新興市場套利交易更加挑剔，並避開以G10貨幣進行這類策略。該行仍看好土耳其里拉等高息貨幣，也認為收益較低的印度盧比可能有不錯表現。
摩根士丹利(MS-US)則預期，新興市場套利交易仍有機會維持良好表現，但建議使用歐元等美元以外的貨幣融資。歐元近來也受到希望避開日元波動的交易員青睞。
摩根資產管理新興市場債券主管Pierre-Yves Bareau已降低套利曝險，但仍分散持有哥倫比亞披索、巴西幣及土耳其里拉等部位，規模則小於年初。
他表示，巴西、埃及與奈及利亞等市場的波動，凸顯投資人必須更加注意風險：「你仍會想參與，但必須非常有紀律。」
paras_en: U.S. equity AI trading has cooled, and the impact is now extending to the foreign‑exchange market. The carry trade, which has previously benefited from interest‑rate differentials, economic resilience and a low‑volatility environment, is now facing a test. Although some strategies posted returns near 20% earlier this year, Wall Street believes the easy‑profit phase may be over as market turbulence intensifies.

According to Bloomberg, a carry trade involves investors borrowing low‑yielding currencies such as the yen, euro or dollar and investing the proceeds in higher‑yielding assets to capture the spread. However, if the target currency depreciates, exchange‑rate losses can quickly erode the accrued interest earnings.
Carry trades can still be profitable, but Wall Street warns that they cannot be set‑and‑forgotten.

Over the past year-plus, ample spreads, solid economic growth, rising equity markets and prolonged low volatility allowed carry trades to perform even amid turmoil from the Iran war, yen interventions and Turkey’s political scandal.

Tracy Chen, portfolio manager at Brandywine Global Investment Management, said, “The easiest phase to make money on this trade may have passed. I’m not saying carry trades are finished, but the threshold to hold these positions has risen.”

Carry trades remain profitable overall. Bloomberg data show that, as of Tuesday, a basket of emerging‑market positions funded with euros has returned 13% year‑to‑date, while dollar‑funded strategies have delivered about 18% over the past two years. Those returns have narrowed in recent weeks, and managers are more cautious about whether the strategy can shine again in 2027.

Goldman Sachs (GS-US) believes that after years of strong performance, the upside potential for carry trades has become more limited. Citi’s (C-US) U.S. FX trading team cautions that carry trades should not be treated as a set‑and‑forget position.

The Brazilian real exemplifies how risk can surface quickly. Double‑digit local rates once made Brazil a popular carry‑trade destination, but after President Lula defeated market‑favored Flavio Bolsonaro in the runoff, the real plunged 8% in a single day – the biggest drop in over 20 years – prompting investors to unwind positions.
Before the runoff, a long‑real/short‑dollar position had generated an 18% return year‑to‑date; by Tuesday the cumulative gain had shrunk to just 0.5%.

Pablo Goldberg, portfolio manager of BlackRock’s (BLK-US) emerging‑market bond team, described carry‑trade profits as “climbing stairs, while the unwind feels like an elevator going down.” He warned that concentration in a single currency requires heightened risk vigilance.

Nevertheless, the conditions that support carry trades have not vanished entirely. Even as U.S. equities have recently slipped, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq‑100 have stayed in positive territory this year, potentially delivering a fourth consecutive year of gains. JPMorgan’s (JPM-US) FX volatility index has risen but remains well below the multi‑month highs seen at the end of March.
JPMorgan strategists expect carry trades to still play a role in 2027, though performance will be more sensitive to equity‑market swings and shifts in expectations for the Fed’s final policy rate.
Consequently, the bank advises investors to pair defensive hedges—such as buying yen and selling New Zealand dollars or Swiss francs—rather than simply betting on spread returns.

Wells Fargo (WFC-US) is more selective on emerging‑market carry trades and avoids using G‑10 currencies for such strategies. The bank remains bullish on high‑yielding currencies like the Turkish lira and sees potential in the lower‑yielding Indian rupee.

Morgan Stanley (MS-US) expects emerging‑market carry trades to continue delivering solid performance, but recommends financing with currencies other than the dollar, such as the euro. The euro has recently attracted traders looking to sidestep yen volatility.

Pierre‑Yves Bareau, head of emerging‑market bond at Morgan Asset Management, has reduced his carry‑trade exposure but still holds diversified positions in the Colombian peso, Brazilian real and Turkish lira, albeit at a smaller scale than at the start of the year.
He noted that volatility in markets such as Brazil, Egypt and Nigeria underscores the need for greater risk discipline: “You’ll still want to participate, but you have to be very disciplined.”
